description:
We are RSS AstroMinds, a passionate team of students from Rawd Al-Salihin School in Kuwait, guided by our ICT teacher.

Our mission is to develop an innovative health monitoring solution for astronauts during space missions.

We combine creativity, coding, teamwork, and problem-solving to turn ideas into practical solutions. We welcome skills in software development, UI/UX design, data analysis, and space exploration.

Together, we aim to learn, innovate, and make an impact beyond Earth!
summary:
AstroHealth AI is an autonomous astronaut health-monitoring prototype designed for long-duration space missions where communication with Earth may be delayed or unavailable.

Our platform simulates continuous wearable telemetry for four astronauts, monitoring heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, blood pressure, and activity. It combines physical health monitoring, psychological wellbeing check-ins, historical trend analysis, and explainable risk alerts within an interactive mission-control dashboard.

A deterministic risk-detection engine identifies potential concerns using illustrative thresholds, while a Gemini-powered AI assistant helps astronauts and medical officers explore historical changes, compare trends, discuss concerns, and generate personalized example daily routines.

Built using JavaScript, IndexedDB, and offline-first web technologies, AstroHealth AI keeps core monitoring features operational without internet connectivity. AI-powered conversations require connectivity to the Gemini service.

Inspired by NASA’s research on human spaceflight hazards, the project explores how autonomous, explainable monitoring could support future crew health management.

All measurements are synthetic, and the system is an educational prototype rather than a clinically validated medical device.
details:
AstroHealth AI — Autonomous Astronaut Health Monitoring

AstroHealth AI is an offline-first astronaut health monitoring prototype designed for long-duration space missions where communication with Earth may be delayed.

The platform simulates live wearable measurements for four astronauts, including heart rate, SpO₂, blood pressure, and activity. It combines physical health monitoring, psychological wellbeing check-ins, historical analysis, and explainable alerts.

A deterministic risk engine evaluates synthetic measurements against demonstration thresholds and generates traceable alerts. Astronauts can review their personal data, while medical officers can monitor the crew through a dedicated dashboard.

A Gemini-powered AI assistant helps users analyze historical trends, compare time periods, and create illustrative daily routines.

Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, IndexedDB, and a Node.js AI backend, the application supports offline monitoring, while Gemini features require internet connectivity.

Inspired by NASA research on human spaceflight hazards, AstroHealth AI explores how autonomous monitoring could support crew health management.

All measurements are synthetic. The system is an educational prototype, not a clinically validated medical device.
